target: Qiyu MIX A081, Debian qcom-see IIO with original SEE firmware and registry
purpose: Real IIO samples into QVR external-sensor SDK; no synthetic input, hardware access, kernel change or bridge change performed for this investigation.

result.convention: Each output Android axis names its signed 1-based input IIO axis: Android x=+IIO x, y=+IIO y, z=+IIO z.
result.claim: The current Debian IIO driver and original Android sensors HAL preserve the same ordered sns_std_sensor_event data[0..2] as xyz. No additional fixed swap, sign flip or rotation is needed between those software frames.
result.not_inferred_from: trinity sensor_orientation identity; this conclusion follows from the actual Android HAL event conversion and current qcom-see source.
preconditions: The device continues using the original A081 SEE firmware and compatible original ICM4x6xx registry configuration.
The IIO source is qcom-see accel/gyro backed by the ordinary sns_std_sensor_event ID 1025, not a different raw chip-coordinate source.
Read axes in x,y,z order using the actual scan layout and apply the exported IIO scale once.

units.conversion: Android sample[i] = IIO signed integer axis[i] * 0.000001
units.timestamp: QVR external SDK requires Android BOOTTIME nanoseconds; timestamp conversion is a separate contract and is not established by the axis proof.

proof_chain.observation: Field 1 repeated float32 values are consumed sequentially with scan.axis[n++]. see_float_micro preserves each sign and converts to signed micro-SI. see_read_raw reports IIO_VAL_INT_PLUS_MICRO with val=0,val2=1. There is no axis permutation, sign flip or rotation.

proof_chain.stage: Same SEE event to original Android acceleration event
proof_chain.observation: For event ID 0x401, protobuf data backing offsets +8,+12,+16 become Android Event xyz in that order. Calibrated mode subtracts x/y/z biases from the corresponding axes. Uncalibrated mode copies xyz and reports the three biases separately. The enqueued original Event is not modified by can_submit_sample, which receives a separate copy.
code_anchors: lines 117-121: calibrated data[0..2] minus same-axis biases
lines 222-243: gate on a copy and enqueue original xyz

proof_chain.stage: Same SEE event to original Android angular velocity event
proof_chain.observation: For event ID 0x401, data[0..2] likewise becomes Android Event xyz in original order. Calibrated mode only subtracts the respective three bias values; uncalibrated mode copies xyz. Original Event xyz is enqueued after the gate receives a copy.
code_anchors: lines 212-233: gate and original Event enqueue

proof_chain.observation: Copies the queued android::hardware::sensors::V1_0::Event vector directly into the Android FMQ using MessageQueue::MemTransaction::copyTo and signals the event flag. No coordinate conversion is inserted.

Declares float sample[3] in Android portrait orientation, accel m/s/s and gyro rad/s. The relative-frame equality above therefore establishes the required signed permutation for this external input route.

registry.scope: This is an upstream ICM4x6xx SEE-driver registry orientation. The HAL consumes already produced sns_std_sensor_event values without applying it on AP. Do not apply this registry rotation again when adapting the same events from IIO.
registry.limitation: This offline review verified local registry copies, not the current on-device mounted registry. The identity between the two event-conversion paths is independently visible in their code.

observations: sensors_hal::config_direct_report obtains the chosen sensor SUID, period, timestamp offset and sensor handle. Its flags select calibrated versus uncalibrated reporting (observed values 6 and 2). No axis matrix or permutation is passed in this AP setup.

The small SLPI libsns_low_lat_stream_skel.so maps the shared buffer using apps_mem_share_map and forwards configuration to imported sns_llcm_config. The actual low-latency sample writer is resident in firmware and was not decompiled.
direct_channel_scope.limitation: Do not describe the direct-channel firmware sample-copy implementation as fully verified by this analysis. The chosen external SDK route needs the Android sensor event frame, which is directly established by the normal original Android HAL above.
direct_channel_scope.hexagon_decompiler_caution: Hexagon pseudocode can omit register-passed arguments; the low-latency skeleton is used only to establish delegation, not to infer sns_llcm_config prototype or axis handling.

remaining_limits: No physical rotation/optical/world-alignment observation was made in this offline task.
Axis identity is not a claim of equal calibrated numerical values: the stock Android calibrated HAL subtracts sensor-calibration biases while qcom-see currently forwards the raw SEE sample.
Current live firmware/registry equivalence is an input precondition; no device access occurred.
No complete OpenXR positional tracking or sensor-to-camera timing validation is implied.

hal_guards_valid_results_only.excluded_failed_request: The guessed mangled can_submit_sample name failed lookup; no conclusion relies on a decompile of that function.
